A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUMMQ research. Their text, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original summarization experiments on MENSA, BookSum, and GovReport, alongside human evaluations, ablations, and agent-configuration analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports token consumption and monetary costs on MENSA.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same generation, aggregation, voting, review, debate, and examinee procedures. The detailed agent prompts are unchanged, moving from Appendix F to G.

E1.justification: Both versions use MENSA, BookSum, GovReport, and the same 20 NLP papers for human evaluation. The added cost analysis uses existing MENSA coverage with GPT-4o.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the benchmark, backbone, human, and LLM-judge comparisons is unchanged. The new cost comparison reuses GPT-4o prompting and the existing SUMMQsolo and SUMMQcombo configurations.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds resource-evaluation metrics: average input tokens, output tokens, and USD cost per MENSA example with GPT-4o. Existing quality metrics, agent and iteration settings, judge procedures, and human-evaluation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a supplementary analysis comparing the computational burden of prompting, SUMMQsolo, and SUMMQcombo. Existing component, iteration, agent-count, quizzing, mixed-backbone, quiz-coverage, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new cost table supplies averages without adding uncertainty estimates or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports per-example costs of $0.18, $1.95, and $14.45 for prompting, SUMMQsolo, and SUMMQcombo, respectively, alongside token totals. Existing benchmark scores, ablation results, evaluation figures, and case-study outputs are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and operations in Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit code-release claim. The scientific claims about the adversarial framework, three-benchmark evaluation, performance superiority, and agent-collaboration analyses retain their original scope.

C2.justification: v1 already discusses diminishing returns and increased computational cost. New Appendix D attributes measured overhead to iterative multi-agent collaboration and argues that the expense is justified for applications prioritizing output quality over efficiency.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, identifies the Baskerville computing facility, and reports resource consumption. Existing algorithms, settings, and prompts remain unchanged. Release timing is inconsistent: the abstract says code is released, while the reproducibility statement promises release upon publication.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier summarization and multi-agent research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds cost-analysis, ethics, reproducibility, LLM-use, and acknowledgement sections, plus a short abstract addition and affiliation updates. The existing scientific prose and narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the cost table, repositions Algorithms 1–3, and rearranges appendix material. The human-evaluation paper list and case-study table become Tables 9 and 10; existing figures and result-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: New Table 8 makes the previously qualitative computational-cost tradeoff assessable, and the repository pointer and computing disclosure improve transparency. Existing methods and quality evidence are retained. The inconsistent code-release timing limits the reproducibility benefit, but the added cost evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
